vortex-dynamics/aerospace-division/vd;-a.title: VD; Aerospace division
vortex-dynamics/aerospace-division/vd;-a.description:
Atmospheric Vehicle DivisionAttack (A)Utility (U)Remote controlled (Q)Multi role (M)Helicopter (H)Cargo (C)Fighters (F)Drop ships (D)UD-47AThe most common variant. It comes with a chin gun and pylons, and can be used to move infantry and or cargoUD-47CThe fire support variant. its Bay has been extremely modified to allow the fitting of heavy weapons.UD-47CIVThe civilian the airframe. These were built with many different attachment points to allow it to be sold to many different industries.UD-47BThe vehicle transport variant
is missing the Bay and is instead replaced with clamps and attachment points To load a vehicle onto the back.UD-47The prototype airframe. Only five of these were produced and they proved to do exactly what was needed, winning Vortex dynamics the contract.F/A-80The prototype airframe, It could barely fly when it was first made but after a few different variations it proved itself and production was started.F/A-80AThe single seater variant of the airframe, It only has a singular pilot. Has a slightly higher fuel capacity than the twin seater variantF/A-80BThe twin seater version of the airframe, it has pilot and a WSO, Has a slightly lower fuel capacity then the single seater variant.The F/A-80 was then made into two nearly identical airframes with the only difference being one is a twin seater and one is a solo seater variant.Recon (R)The aircraft being the twin seater variant is generally more effective than the solo variant. One reason for this is the fact that the pilot and the WSO Can both use the weapons on the aircraft at the same time. In situations where a fight quickly goes from BVR To a dog fight The aircraft can engage two targets instead of justice one. Most weapon systems can be slaved to the HMCS Which also helps with the dual weapon system use.The aircraft has a reduced load for the pilot because it can be shared with WSO, This lowers air crews suicide rates greatly by also giving them a friend in stressful situations.F/A-80TThe trainer variant, it's used to teach people the basic controls of the airframe. Used to teach people all F/A-80 Airframes.Exoatmospheric Vehicle DivisionWeapons DivisionAGM (Air-to-ground missile)AIM (Air intercept missile)GBU (Guided bomb unit)LAU (Launch air unit)ALQ (Frequency jammer)AIM-22A medium range air to air missile with active radar homing and the ability to be redirected to a target after Pitbull.A medium range air to air missile with active radar homing and the ability to be redirected to a target after Pitbull.

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
